chapters.title: The recognition gap
chapters.dek: We built places to publish and places to store. GestaltView asks what it takes to keep a person’s context intact while they think, change, and make things.

chapters.title: Capture and rooms
chapters.story_title: A thought gets somewhere safe to land
chapters.dek: First it can be held without being sorted. From there, the person—not a filing rule—decides whether it belongs in a room, a scaffold, or a future creation.

chapters.title: Memory and continuity
chapters.story_title: Memory is more than finding a similar sentence
chapters.dek: The wiki separates raw material, knowledge fragments, temporal context, identity, and retrieval. The distinctions matter because a human life is not a nearest-neighbor query.

chapters.title: Billy and collaboration
chapters.story_title: Help is a system of roles, not one magic box
chapters.dek: Billy, skills, embodiment, routing, and specialized Digital Intelligences have different responsibilities. The architecture is meant to coordinate them, not pretend one voice does everything.

chapters.title: Creation and artifacts
chapters.story_title: An artifact passes through a gate before it leaves
chapters.dek: Captures can become plans and outputs, but rendering has stages, checks, and review. The pipeline diagram marks where the system must stop and ask what is allowed.

chapters.title: Governance and evidence
chapters.story_title: Safety is part of the architecture
chapters.dek: Invariants, evaluation, access controls, and evidence are drawn as system boundaries—not as a reassuring paragraph appended after the exciting bit.

chapters.title: The map behind the map
chapters.story_title: The filing cabinet, with its drawers labeled
chapters.dek: Repository topology, documentation graphs, and source maps show where responsibilities live and how a reader can trace a claim back to its home.
